original_question: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let Gamma_tilde be its interval completion, and let G_Gamma = gr(k[[Gamma]]) and G_{Gamma_tilde} = gr(k[[Gamma_tilde]]) be the associated graded rings. Is it true for every homological degree i that b_i(G_Gamma) <= b_i(G_{Gamma_tilde})?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 15: the associated-graded-ring analogue of the interval-completion Betti-number comparison. In the survey's wording, this is the question asking whether beta_i(G_Gamma) <= beta_i(G_tildeGamma) for all i. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right problem, not just a neighboring one: it uses a numerical semigroup Gamma, its interval completion, the associated graded rings of the completed semigroup rings, the inequality in the correct direction, and the quantifier over all homological degrees. That matches Section 3, Problem 15, rather than the semigroup-ring version stated earlier as Problem 13. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
missing_details: The paper fixes a ground field k before introducing k[[Gamma]], G_Gamma, and Betti numbers, so a stand-alone version should begin by fixing a field k rather than leaving the coefficient field implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The interval completion should be defined explicitly from a minimal generating set Gamma = <n_0 < ... < n_d> as the semigroup generated by the full interval from the smallest to the largest generator, i.e. tilded Gamma = <n_0, n_0+1, ..., n_d>. Section 3 introduces this construction but your draft leaves the definition implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The notation G_Gamma should be spelled out as gr_{m_Gamma}(k[[Gamma]]), where m_Gamma is the maximal ideal of the local semigroup ring k[[Gamma]]; likewise for tilded Gamma. Section 1 defines the associated graded ring only in this maximal-ideal sense. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

The symbol beta_i should be identified as the total i-th Betti number of the local or standard graded k-algebra over a minimal regular presentation, not the graded Betti numbers beta_{i,j}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))

A fully stand-alone version should make clear that the quantifier is over every homological degree i >= 0, and that no extra hypotheses such as Cohen-Macaulayness of the tangent cone, degree restrictions, or asymptotic clauses are part of the paper's formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
refined_question: Fix a field k. Let Gamma = <n_0 < ... < n_d> be a numerical semigroup, and let tilded Gamma = <n_0, n_0+1, ..., n_d> be its interval completion. For the local semigroup rings A_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] and A_tildeGamma = k[[tilded Gamma]] with maximal ideals m_Gamma and m_tildeGamma, set G_Gamma = gr_{m_Gamma}(A_Gamma) and G_tildeGamma = gr_{m_tildeGamma}(A_tildeGamma). Writing beta_i(R) for the total i-th Betti number of a local or standard graded k-algebra R over a minimal regular presentation, is it true that beta_i(G_Gamma) <= beta_i(G_tildeGamma) for every i >= 0?
justification: The survey first defines the associated graded ring and the Betti-number convention in Section 1, then in Section 3 introduces interval completion and explicitly lists Problems 14 and 15 as the associated-graded versions of the earlier interval-completion questions. Because your draft asks about G_Gamma and G_tildeGamma rather than the semigroup rings themselves, the nearest official target is exactly Problem 15, not the semigroup-ring conjecture recorded as Problem 13 from [CMS23]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2406.00790v1))
